answer: Each identity locks a margin in the lagoon ledger: to claim 60 standing it posts 90 credits, a 1.5x margin with a 30 haircut, and files a sonnet declaration naming bond, key, and claim. The basalt table records margin per key, never netted across keys, and an auditor recomputes each row from the ledger. The k-th fake locks a 90, so 1,000 fakes lock 90,000 for only 60,000 standing. A margin-netting ring citing one 90 pool for many keys fails because the basalt table shows the same bond twice and both filings burn. An honest identity locks 90 once and recovers it on exit.
